title: Parameter for `st.columns` to disable column stacking on mobiles
body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests. - [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue. ### Summary Many people try to make websites with Streamlit that work on **mobile devices**. But when they try to use `st.columns` to build beautiful layouts, they are frustrated to find it **stacked vertically** on mobile screens. This layout: Instead of this one: ### Why? To make it convenient to use Streamlit apps from mobile devices or tablets. ### How? It would be amazing to have a parameter called `disable_colmn_stacking` in `st.columns` to force that column to be displayed vertically. Maybe detect if it will overflow the screen; in this case, make it stack vertically, or let it overflow if it will as it is the developer's choice. Before: After: ### Additional Context Hope to fix this problem ASAP. Thank you for your efforts. Best regards.

**To help Streamlit prioritize this feature, react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your vote helps us identify which enhancements matter most to our users.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-16056)

This is a **feature request** (`type:enhancement`) asking for a way to control the automatic responsive behavior of `st.columns`, which currently stacks columns vertically on narrow (mobile/tablet) viewports. The proposal is a parameter (e.g. `disable_column_stacking`) to force columns to stay side-by-side, optionally allowing horizontal overflow instead of stacking.

The responsive stacking is intentional behavior implemented on the frontend: in `StyledColumn` (`frontend/lib/src/components/core/Block/styled-components.ts`), a media query forces each column's `min-width` to roughly `100%` once the viewport drops below the `breakpoints.columns` threshold, so columns wrap onto their own rows. Any implementation of this request would need to expose an option to skip/override that media rule (and decide between overflow vs. horizontal scrolling). This is a highly requested, long-standing enhancement rather than a bug, so it likely needs product input on the API surface (a per-call parameter vs. a global config, and how it interacts with the existing flex/wrap layout system).

### Related Issues

- [#5003 – Deactivate responsiveness of `st.columns`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5003): Near-duplicate and the most upvoted version of this request. Same core ask: prevent `st.columns` from collapsing/stacking vertically on mobile and allow forcing a horizontal layout.
- [#6592 – Configurable column responsiveness width threshold](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6592): Closely related — instead of fully disabling stacking, it asks to configure the width threshold at which columns wrap, giving developers control over the same responsive behavior.
- [#12582 – Control wrap behavior for horizontal `st.container`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12582): Related mechanism — requests disabling flex wrapping so horizontal elements stay in a single row, which is the same underlying flex-wrap behavior that causes columns to stack.
